newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures end pre-holiday trade weak.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures end pre-holiday trade weak.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended pre-holiday pit trading mostly weaker, after the long end shut early before Monday's U.S. Veteran's Day holiday.
Treasury bond futures shut early on Friday, but Eurodollar futures observed normal hours.
Chicago Mercantile Exchange financial futures will shut at noon on November 11. Chicago Board of Trade financial products including U.S. Treasury bond futures will be closed on Monday.
On Friday, December T-bond futures again stalled at 114-17/32, just shy of 114-18/32, the 61.8-percent retracement of the 10-month downmove.
Technicians noted that the mid-114 area has proved increasing resistant to upmoves in nearby T-bond futures, although some called Friday's close just above 114-00 fairly neutral.
"It's (close) not bad, it's not good," said one floor broker. "Net-net, it's probably okay."
The market had broken down to the day's low in a barrage of selling from one dealer, seen selling at least 4,000 December T-bonds from 114-08/32 on down.
Some brokers later tied that pullback to a rumor, quickly denied, that President Clinton had been shot.
Some brokers also linked weakness to the 1.3-pct drop in September U.S. wholesale inventories. Traders had expected inventories to rise 0.3 percent.
They argued that the drawdown in inventories was unintentional and thus would require manufacturers to crank up production to replenish.
Others, however, countered that the drawdown might have been intentional, in preparation for an economic slowdown.
December T-bonds fell 7/32 to 114-02/32, T-notes eased 3/32 to 110-05/32, munis lost 4/32 to 116-21/32, March T-bills fell two bps to 94.94, Eurodollars ended off one bp 94.45.
